title: Your introduction to AI & ChatGPT
subtitle: Build a shared vocabulary — what AI is, what ChatGPT does, and which plan fits which work.
benefit: Start with the basics so every conversation builds on the same foundation.
why: Understand the difference between AI, generative AI, and ChatGPT.
Know which ChatGPT plan fits which kind of work.
Build a shared vocabulary before going hands-on.
prompt: Explain in 100 words what generative AI is, how it differs from traditional automation, and three examples I would see in my daily work. Keep it simple. Add 2 myths to avoid.
challenge: Spend 10 minutes asking ChatGPT three questions about your role, and note what felt useful versus what felt wrong.
card04Text: Never paste confidential, customer, or financial data into any AI tool until IT has approved it for company use.

title: Meet ChatGPT: your everyday work partner
subtitle: Learn how to ask better questions, refine answers, and turn rough notes into useful first drafts.
benefit: Draft, rewrite, summarise, explain, brainstorm, translate, and plan faster.
why: Use a simple prompt formula: role, task, context, output, tone.
Improve email, report, and meeting preparation quality.
Turn blank-page work into a faster first draft.
prompt: Act as a professional communications assistant. Rewrite the message below to be clearer, warmer, and concise. Keep the meaning unchanged. Message: [paste text].
challenge: Use ChatGPT to rewrite one internal message into a clearer version before sending it.
card04Text: Review every AI output before sharing. You own the final message and judgement.

title: Prompt better, get better results
subtitle: Workshop month: practise hands-on prompting and learn how to guide ChatGPT with clear context and constraints.
benefit: Better prompts reduce rework and help AI produce more useful answers.
why: Learn the difference between vague and strong prompts.
Practise prompt refinement and follow-up questions.
Build your personal library of reusable prompts.
prompt: Act as an expert prompt coach. Improve this prompt for a business audience and explain what you changed and why: [paste prompt].
challenge: Create five reusable prompts for your role and share one with your team.
card04Text: Join the live workshop to practise prompt refinement with your team this month.

title: Write faster and communicate clearly
subtitle: Use AI to make messages clearer, more professional, and more audience-ready.
benefit: Reduce drafting time while improving clarity, tone, and structure.
why: Create first drafts for emails, memos, agendas, and summaries.
Adjust tone for customers, managers, or cross-functional teams.
Turn bullet points into a polished update.
prompt: Turn these bullet points into a professional update for senior management. Keep it concise, action-oriented, and easy to scan: [paste bullets].
challenge: Take one rough note and ask ChatGPT to turn it into a polished email or short report.
card04Text: Check facts, names, commitments, and dates manually before sending.

title: From information overload to clarity
subtitle: Use AI to summarise documents, compare options, and prepare decision-ready notes.
benefit: Read faster, extract key points, and convert long material into useful action.
why: Summarise policies, reports, meeting notes, or articles.
Ask for pros, cons, risks, and open questions.
Create comparison tables for better decisions.
prompt: Summarise this document for a busy manager. Include: 5 key points, 3 risks, 3 actions, and questions we should clarify. Text: [paste content].
challenge: Summarise one non-confidential document into a one-page brief.
card04Text: Verify facts, sources, and dates. AI summaries can miss nuance or overstate certainty.

title: Make data easier to understand
subtitle: Workshop month: learn how AI can help explain trends, compare figures, and turn data into business commentary.
benefit: Move from raw numbers to clearer insights, faster.
why: Ask questions about spreadsheet trends and variances.
Create first-draft commentary for reports.
Spot outliers, missing data, and follow-up questions.
prompt: Act as a business analyst. Review the data below and produce: key trends, possible reasons, risks, and recommended next actions. Data: [paste table].
challenge: Bring a sample non-confidential dataset or report and create a one-page insight summary.
card04Text: Bring a dataset to the workshop and turn it into a one-page commentary together.

title: AI for every team, not just IT
subtitle: Identify practical AI use cases across HR, Finance, Sales, Operations, Customer Service, IT, and leadership.
benefit: The biggest value appears when AI solves real department pain points.
why: Map recurring tasks that involve drafting, reviewing, summarising, or analysing.
Prioritise use cases by value, frequency, and risk.
Create team-specific prompt packs.
prompt: Act as an AI use-case consultant. For this department, suggest 10 practical AI use cases ranked by value, effort, and risk. Department: [name].
challenge: Submit three use cases from your department using the use-case template.
card04Text: Escalate high-risk use cases involving customers, HR, finance, legal, safety, or compliance.

title: Redesign the work, not just the tools
subtitle: Use AI to improve processes, SOPs, checklists, FAQs, and repeatable workflows.
benefit: Reduce manual effort and make work more consistent across teams.
why: Turn informal know-how into standard checklists.
Improve SOP clarity and handover quality.
Find bottlenecks in repetitive processes.
prompt: Review this process and suggest how AI can support each step. Show the current step, AI support, human review point, and expected benefit. Process: [paste process].
challenge: Pick one workflow and map where AI can help draft, review, summarise, or analyse.
card04Text: Keep humans responsible for approval points and final decisions.

title: Build, test, and share real use cases
subtitle: Workshop month: departments turn ideas into reusable prompt workflows and lightweight pilots.
benefit: Adoption grows faster when practical examples are shared by trusted colleagues.
why: Select high-value, low-risk use cases.
Build prompt flows and reusable templates.
Create simple success measures such as time saved or quality improved.
prompt: Help me turn this AI use case into a repeatable prompt workflow. Include inputs, prompt steps, output format, human review, and success metric. Use case: [describe].
challenge: Create one department prompt workflow and test it with sample information.
card04Text: Champions cohort meets this month — share your pilot and learn from peers.

title: Use AI safely and confidently
subtitle: Strengthen governance: privacy, accuracy, fairness, human review, and clear accountability.
benefit: Good governance helps people use AI with confidence instead of uncertainty.
why: Know what data should never be entered into AI tools.
Use a simple risk checklist before high-impact tasks.
Build human review into every AI-assisted workflow.
prompt: Act as a responsible AI reviewer. Assess this proposed AI use case for privacy, accuracy, bias, compliance, and human review risks. Use case: [describe].
challenge: Review one team use case with the responsible AI checklist.
card04Text: For sensitive or regulated topics, get the right review before using AI outputs.

title: From productivity to possibility
subtitle: Use AI to generate new ideas, test scenarios, and design better customer or employee experiences.
benefit: AI can help us improve existing work and imagine new ways to deliver value.
why: Brainstorm service improvements and customer experience ideas.
Run scenario planning and role-play objections.
Prototype training, communication, or process improvements faster.
prompt: Act as an innovation facilitator. Generate 10 AI-enabled improvement ideas for this business challenge. For each, show benefit, effort, risk, and first experiment. Challenge: [describe].
challenge: Propose one AI-enabled improvement idea and define a small experiment.
card04Text: Treat AI ideas as starting points. Validate feasibility, cost, customer impact, and risk.

title: Celebrate progress and scale impact
subtitle: Workshop month: share success stories, measure impact, and choose the next AI priorities.
benefit: AI readiness becomes sustainable when value is measured and successful practices are scaled.
why: Showcase department wins and lessons learned.
Measure adoption, confidence, time saved, and quality gains.
Agree the Year 2 roadmap for deeper AI adoption.
prompt: Help me write a concise AI success story using this structure: problem, AI support, human review, result, lesson learned, next step. Notes: [paste content].
challenge: Submit one AI success story or lesson learned from your team.
card04Text: Year-end showcase — present your AI win and shape the Year 2 roadmap.

title: From skill to system
subtitle: Set Year 2 priorities and move from individual AI skills to team workflows.
benefit: Year 2 turns personal practice into shared department systems.
why: Review Year 1 wins and gaps per team.
Set 2–3 measurable AI goals per department.
Identify the one workflow each team will rebuild around AI.
prompt: Act as our AI program lead. Help me draft 3 Year-2 AI goals for [department] that are specific, measurable, and tied to a business outcome. Constraints: [resources, timeline].
challenge: Submit your department's three Year 2 AI goals using the goal template.
card04Text: Goals should improve work, not pressure colleagues into unsafe AI use. Keep human review in every workflow.

title: AI for finance and reporting
subtitle: Use AI to speed up variance commentary, draft reports, and explore "what if" scenarios.
benefit: AI helps finance teams move from data wrangling to insight and decision support.
why: Draft variance and management commentary from raw numbers.
Build "what if" scenarios for budgets and forecasts.
Generate clear narratives for non-finance leaders.
prompt: Act as a finance business partner. Read the numbers below and write a one-page management commentary covering trends, drivers, risks, and recommended actions. Data: [paste].
challenge: Take one routine finance report and AI-draft the commentary, then refine it.
card04Text: Never paste customer, vendor, or restricted financial data into a non-approved AI tool. Use anonymised or aggregated inputs.

title: AI for HR — from JDs to onboarding
subtitle: Workshop month: hands-on HR use cases — job descriptions, interview questions, policy Q&A, onboarding kits.
benefit: HR can move faster while keeping every touchpoint fair, clear, and human.
why: Draft inclusive, accurate job descriptions in minutes.
Generate competency-based interview questions and scoring guides.
Build onboarding plans and policy explainers employees actually read.
prompt: Act as a Goldbell HR partner. Draft a job description for [role] including purpose, key outcomes, must-have skills, nice-to-haves, and an inclusive language check. Context: [details].
challenge: Rebuild one job description or onboarding doc with AI and ask a peer for honest feedback.
card04Text: HR cohort workshop — bring a real (anonymised) HR task and rebuild it with AI.

title: AI for sales — outreach to objections
subtitle: Help sales teams research accounts, personalise outreach, and rehearse difficult conversations.
benefit: AI helps salespeople spend more time talking to customers and less time staring at blank screens.
why: Research accounts and contacts faster from public information.
Personalise outreach without sounding generic.
Rehearse pricing, scope, and objection conversations before they happen.
prompt: Act as my sales coach. Given this account profile, draft a personalised outreach email and three follow-up touchpoints. Then list five objections likely to come up and how I should respond. Account: [paste].
challenge: Pick one stalled opportunity. Have AI generate a refreshed approach and try it this week.
card04Text: Outputs are drafts, not commitments. Always check price, scope, and policy details before sending.

title: AI for service — clearer, faster, kinder
subtitle: Build response templates, sentiment triage, and escalation drafts for service teams.
benefit: Service teams respond faster while keeping every message warm and on-brand.
why: Draft macros and reply templates for common issues.
Detect tone and prioritise upset or urgent customers.
Draft escalation summaries with context, options, and recommendations.
prompt: Act as a senior customer-service lead. Read this customer message and draft a reply that acknowledges, explains, offers a next step, and ends warmly. Then assess sentiment and urgency. Message: [paste].
challenge: Take one tough customer message this week and use AI to draft the first response — then a human edits.
card04Text: Never share account details, IDs, or personal information with AI. Use placeholders and edit in the final reply.

title: AI for operations — playbooks and incidents
subtitle: Workshop month: rebuild SOPs, incident reports, and supplier communications with AI support.
benefit: Operations becomes more consistent when knowledge stops living in people's heads.
why: Convert tribal knowledge into clear SOPs and checklists.
Draft incident reports and root-cause notes quickly.
Generate supplier and partner communications consistently.
prompt: Act as an ops continuous-improvement lead. Given these notes from a recent incident, draft an incident report with: summary, timeline, root cause hypothesis, immediate fix, and prevention actions. Notes: [paste].
challenge: Pick one informal process. Rebuild it as a clear AI-assisted SOP and circulate for feedback.
card04Text: Operations cohort — bring one SOP or incident note to rebuild together.

title: AI for procurement and supply
subtitle: Use AI to compare quotes, summarise contracts, and prepare supplier conversations.
benefit: AI speeds up procurement analysis so teams can negotiate from a stronger position.
why: Compare quotes and vendor proposals side by side.
Summarise long contracts and flag unusual clauses.
Prepare structured supplier review and negotiation notes.
prompt: Act as a senior procurement analyst. Compare these three vendor proposals side by side on price, scope, terms, risks, and recommended next questions. Proposals: [paste].
challenge: Use AI to summarise one supplier contract and prepare three questions for your next review.
card04Text: Contract terms must be confirmed by Legal or Finance. AI summaries are a starting point, not the source of truth.

title: AI for leaders — decisions and memos
subtitle: Practical AI uses for managers and leaders: decision memos, board updates, town hall scripts.
benefit: Leaders get more thinking time when AI handles the heavy drafting work.
why: Draft decision memos with options, trade-offs, and recommendations.
Generate board and exco updates from raw notes.
Prepare town hall and team communications in different tones.
prompt: Act as my chief of staff. Turn these meeting notes into a one-page decision memo with context, options, trade-offs, recommendation, and risks. Notes: [paste].
challenge: Take one upcoming decision and draft the memo with AI. Bring it to your next 1:1 for review.
card04Text: Strategic and people-sensitive content should never go through public AI tools. Use approved internal tools only.

title: AI for marketing — briefs to campaigns
subtitle: Workshop month: campaign briefs, content variants, social posts, landing-page drafts.
benefit: Marketing teams can produce more variants and test ideas without burning out.
why: Generate campaign briefs and creative concepts faster.
Produce on-brand content variants for different channels.
Test landing-page and email copy options before launch.
prompt: Act as our brand-trained marketing strategist. Draft a campaign brief for [product] that includes objective, audience, key message, three creative concepts, channels, and measurement. Context: [paste].
challenge: Pick one campaign and AI-generate three concept directions. Choose one to develop with your team.
card04Text: Marketing cohort — bring a real brief and run it through AI for fresh angles.

title: AI for meetings — transcribe, summarise, act
subtitle: Use AI tools to capture meetings, summarise outcomes, and assign next actions automatically.
benefit: Meetings become more useful when notes, decisions, and actions are captured by default.
why: Transcribe meetings accurately and securely.
Auto-summarise decisions, actions, owners, and dates.
Convert long calls into one-page briefings.
prompt: Act as my executive assistant. From this meeting transcript, produce a one-page summary with: context, decisions, action items with owners and dates, open questions, and follow-up suggestions. Transcript: [paste].
challenge: Use AI to summarise one internal meeting this week and share the action list with attendees.
card04Text: Only record meetings when participants are informed and consent. Avoid external or client meetings unless permitted by policy.

title: Connect AI to the tools you already use
subtitle: Bring AI into email, Teams, SharePoint, and everyday productivity tools.
benefit: AI delivers value where work happens, not in a separate browser tab.
why: Use Copilot or equivalent AI features inside Outlook, Word, Excel, Teams.
Connect AI to internal knowledge stores safely.
Replace some manual lookups with AI-assisted search.
prompt: Act as a Microsoft 365 productivity coach. For [my role], suggest 10 ways to use Copilot inside Outlook, Word, Excel, Teams, and PowerPoint, ranked by impact and ease. Constraints: [policy notes].
challenge: Pick one tool you already use and try one AI feature inside it this week.
card04Text: In integrated AI tools, your data may be processed by the vendor. Confirm what is and isn't permitted under Goldbell IT policy.

title: Department playbooks and the road ahead
subtitle: Workshop month: each department shares its AI playbook and Year 3 priorities.
benefit: Year 2 ends with shared playbooks that anyone in a role can adopt on day one.
why: Document each team's standard AI workflows.
Compare adoption, time saved, and quality gains across teams.
Choose where to scale, automate, or pause.
prompt: Help me draft my department's AI playbook. Include: roles, top 5 workflows, prompts used, success measures, risks, and what we still need help with. Notes: [paste].
challenge: Submit your department's Year 2 AI playbook draft for the showcase.
card04Text: Year 2 showcase — present your playbook and vote on Year 3 priorities.

title: From systems to scale
subtitle: Year 3 moves from team workflows to automated, governed, measurable AI at Goldbell.
benefit: AI shifts from "extra effort" to "default way we work" when it is automated and measured.
why: Identify workflows ready for automation and agents.
Set group-level metrics for AI value and risk.
Plan the move from copy-paste prompts to integrated tools.
prompt: Act as our AI strategy lead. Given Year 1–2 wins and gaps, draft three Year-3 priorities for Goldbell with rationale, owner, target outcome, and a 90-day kickoff plan. Inputs: [paste].
challenge: Submit your department's top automation candidate workflow.
card04Text: Automation amplifies mistakes. Every automated workflow needs an owner, a human review point, and a fallback.

title: Build a custom AI assistant for your team
subtitle: Create low-code custom GPTs, Copilots, or assistants tuned to your team's tasks and knowledge.
benefit: Custom assistants are faster than prompts because the context is built in.
why: Identify a high-frequency, well-defined task to wrap into a custom assistant.
Pre-load context, examples, and guardrails.
Roll out, gather feedback, and improve weekly.
prompt: Act as a custom GPT designer. For this task, propose the assistant's role, system prompt, sample inputs, guardrails, allowed and forbidden behaviours, and three test scenarios. Task: [describe].
challenge: Spec one custom assistant for your team and build a first version this month.
card04Text: Custom assistants must follow Goldbell data-handling rules. Get IT and Legal review before any production rollout.

title: AI + automation — trigger to outcome
subtitle: Workshop month: build end-to-end flows with AI triggers (Power Automate, n8n, Make, Zapier).
benefit: AI plus automation moves work from your inbox to a system that just runs.
why: Map a real workflow with manual and AI steps.
Add triggers, AI generation, human review, and notifications.
Measure before/after time, error rate, and exception cases.
prompt: Act as an automation architect. Design an end-to-end flow for [workflow]: triggers, AI steps, human review, success paths, error paths, and metrics. Constraints: [tools available].
challenge: Pick one workflow and prototype it with AI + your team's automation tool.
card04Text: Automation lab — build one working flow during the workshop with mentor support.

title: Extract structure from PDFs, Excel, and email
subtitle: Use AI to extract key data, fields, and tables from unstructured documents.
benefit: Tasks that used to take hours of copy-paste become a structured table in minutes.
why: Extract fields and tables from invoices, contracts, claims, or forms.
Route extracted data into spreadsheets or systems automatically.
Catch missing or inconsistent values before they cause issues downstream.
prompt: Act as a document intelligence specialist. Extract the following fields from this document into a clean table: [list fields]. Flag any missing, ambiguous, or unusual values. Document: [paste or attach].
challenge: Pick one document type your team handles repeatedly. Use AI to extract its fields and review accuracy.
card04Text: Confidential or regulated documents need approved tooling and storage. Confirm with IT before processing at scale.

title: AI for spreadsheets, SQL, and light code
subtitle: Use AI to write formulas, SQL queries, and small scripts even if you are not a developer.
benefit: Non-technical teams can self-serve data questions they used to wait days for.
why: Get help writing Excel and Google Sheets formulas.
Generate safe, read-only SQL queries with explanations.
Build small scripts to clean files or automate repetitive tasks.
prompt: Act as a friendly data engineer. Write a SQL query to answer this question against this schema, explain what each part does, and warn me about anything that could go wrong. Question and schema: [paste].
challenge: Pick one repetitive data task and have AI help you script or formula your way out of it.
card04Text: Always run AI-generated SQL as read-only first. Never run code or queries on production data without review.

title: Prove the value — time, quality, ROI
subtitle: Workshop month: define and track AI impact across time saved, quality, and outcomes.
benefit: Measured AI value earns more investment and trust from leadership.
why: Define meaningful AI impact metrics per workflow.
Capture before-and-after data simply and honestly.
Tell the story of AI value to leaders and peers.
prompt: Act as a measurement coach. For this AI workflow, propose 3 impact metrics, how to baseline, how to track, and how to present the result on one page. Workflow: [describe].
challenge: Submit a one-page impact story for one AI workflow your team uses.
card04Text: Impact lab — bring a workflow and build its measurement plan together.

title: Responsible AI at scale — risk and audit
subtitle: Strengthen AI governance: risk, audit, vendor due diligence, and incident handling.
benefit: A clear governance model lets people use AI fast without taking unsafe shortcuts.
why: Maintain an AI use-case register with risk levels.
Run vendor and tool due diligence consistently.
Define how to handle AI errors, near misses, and incidents.
prompt: Act as our AI risk officer. Assess this AI use case for data, accuracy, compliance, vendor, and human-oversight risks. Recommend mitigations and a review cadence. Use case: [describe].
challenge: Add one of your team's AI workflows to the AI use-case register, with risks and mitigations.
card04Text: For MAS, PDPA, and customer-facing AI, never skip review. When in doubt, escalate before deploying.

title: Build the internal AI community
subtitle: Launch and sustain an AI champions program: people, rituals, recognition, knowledge base.
benefit: AI scales when people support each other, not just when IT delivers tools.
why: Identify AI champions in every team.
Run monthly clinics, demos, and prompt swaps.
Recognise and reward responsible AI wins.
prompt: Act as our AI program designer. Draft the operating model for our AI champions program: roles, rituals, communication, training, recognition, and success measures.
challenge: Nominate or volunteer one AI champion from your team and join the next monthly clinic.
card04Text: Champions support adoption, not replace governance. Risk decisions still go through the right channels.

title: AI that customers actually see
subtitle: Workshop month: customer-facing AI — chatbots, smart search, AI in apps and the customer portal.
benefit: Done right, customer-facing AI improves service and brand. Done wrong, it damages both.
why: Pick the right customer journeys for AI to assist.
Design tone, fallback, and escalation to a human.
Measure satisfaction, deflection, and incident rates.
prompt: Act as a customer-experience designer. Map this customer journey, suggest where AI assists and where humans must own the moment, and define metrics and risks. Journey: [describe].
challenge: Pick one customer touchpoint and design a small AI assist with clear human fallback.
card04Text: Customer-facing AI lab — design and pressure-test one use case with peer review.

title: Build, buy, or partner — choosing the right path
subtitle: Decision frameworks for build-vs-buy across AI tools, platforms, and custom solutions.
benefit: Smart build-vs-buy decisions avoid wasted spend and tech debt.
why: Score AI options on fit, cost, risk, and time-to-value.
Avoid duplicating what existing platforms already provide.
Decide when custom work is worth the long-term cost.
prompt: Act as our build-vs-buy advisor. For this AI need, compare three approaches (off-the-shelf, configure existing platform, custom build) on fit, cost, risk, time-to-value, and lock-in. Need: [describe].
challenge: Pick one AI need your team has and run it through the build-vs-buy framework with leadership.
card04Text: Vendor choices have long tails — data, exit, and dependency risks. Loop in IT, Legal, and Finance early.

title: From projects to portfolio — AI strategy
subtitle: Align the AI roadmap with business strategy, prioritise across the group, and plan investment.
benefit: AI strategy stops being a list of pilots and becomes part of the business plan.
why: Map AI initiatives to business goals across Goldbell.
Prioritise across value, feasibility, and risk.
Allocate budget, talent, and capacity intentionally.
prompt: Act as our AI strategy advisor. Given these business goals and current AI initiatives, propose a 12-month AI portfolio plan with priorities, sequencing, owners, and success metrics. Inputs: [paste].
challenge: Submit a one-page department AI roadmap that ties to Goldbell business goals.
card04Text: Strategic plans live in approved tools only. Keep sensitive priorities out of public AI services.

title: Three years on — impact and what's next
subtitle: Workshop month: review the three-year journey, celebrate impact, and shape what comes next.
benefit: A clear 3-year story builds permission and energy for the next chapter of AI at Goldbell.
why: Showcase department impact across the 3-year program.
Recognise champions, teams, and standout use cases.
Decide where AI investment goes next, with confidence.
prompt: Help me write a 3-year AI impact story for Goldbell: what we started with, what changed, the wins, the lessons, the people, and where we are heading next. Inputs: [paste highlights].
challenge: Bring your team's 3-year highlight reel or one-pager to the showcase.
card04Text: 3-year review & awards — present, vote, and shape the next program.
